utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]... The Prosecutor versus Miroslav Kvocka, Zoran Zigic, Mladjo Radic, Dragoljub Prcac, and Milojica Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Before we start, I should apologise for the shortness of the notice you received and for the somewhat peremptory setting of the date. We do try, we certainly have in the past, tried to meet the convenience of everybody concerned. However, with only three courtrooms and six Trial Chambers sitting, they're sitting in two shifts and we can no longer fit these Status Conferences in before or after a Trial Chamber is sitting. So it was either today or sometime late in August. You will understand, then, the troubles we've had. Appearances for the Prosecution, Mr. Staker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, my name is Christopher Staker. I appear today on behalf of the Prosecution with my colleague Miss Kelly Howick. Our case manager for today is Miss Diana Dicklich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Kvocka, can you hear these proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT KVOCKA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We received a message from your counsel, Mr. Simic, apologising for his inability to attend today. He had a previous engagement, actually on behalf of the Tribunal, in Banja Luka, and we understand his inability to attend. He says in the message: "My Defence has no issues to arise," that he plans to visit the Tribunal in the first part of July regarding important matters for future proceedings in the case before the Appeals Chamber. So you will no doubt hear from him when he comes. Counsel for Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. My name is Zoran Jovanovic on behalf of Mladjo Radic as legal advisor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Slobodan Stojanovic. Today I will represent the Defence of Mr. Zigic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And for Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Jovan Simic, attorney from Belgrade, and I will represent the Defence of Mr. Prcac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, for each of the other three appellants, are you able to hear the proceedings in a language which you can understand? Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT RADIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZIGIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRCAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, this is Status Conference held in accordance with Rule 65 bis. Are there any matters which the Prosecution wants to raise, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Your Honour, none other than one perhaps very minor technical matter. We note simply the withdrawal of the appeal by the appellant Kos. My reading of the Rules doesn't indicate to me clearly whether a notice of withdrawal is to be regarded as ipso facto effective or whether some kind of order or formal taking of note by the Chamber is required but perhaps this might be an opportunity simply to formalise that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that's been a matter of some discussion. The Registry, as you can imagine, being the Registry, suggested that we should grant leave to withdraw, and I said, "What? Do you mean we can refuse to allow him to withdraw?" There was no answer to that. Another Judge suggested that we should perhaps file a document accepting his withdrawal, but then a minor matter as to whether that was an order or a decision, which apparently is the only things we have power to do, caused that suggestion to go to one side, so we have simply accepted the withdrawal as ipso facto a withdrawal of the appeal, and we have proceeded, you will notice, without any reference to that particular appellant any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you'd got any better suggestions, I'd be grateful for them, but so far, nobody's been able to suggest one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: If we can proceed on the basis that Mr. Kos is no longer a party to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, most certainly, yes. You need not give him notice about anything. The one thing that caused me some concern was in relation to all of these applications by the Prosecution to disclose the material in other proceedings. It may be as well, if you have any further ones - you no doubt will have some further ones - if there was some communication perhaps with his former counsel about it. I would myself feel easier if there was some such record that he had been consulted or someone on his behalf had been consulted, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAKER
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything that any of the appellants wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. There are no issues that the Defence of Mladjo Radic would like to raise at this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, this appeal is somewhat unusual in that it is sailing smoothly ahead without the usual problems about fresh evidence and Rule 68 discovery and things, and it seems that if everything goes well, we should have all of the pre-appeal pleadings completed by the end of July. Now, the prospect of a date is something which is starting to be considered. It looks as if there will be available a slot at the end of October or sometime early in November. It will depend, to a very large extent, as to what happens in the appeal of Mr. Blaskic, which has priority in timing, but the position in relation to that appeal will not be resolved for another week or so. You will be consulted in relation to dates. The Appeals Chamber is able to have some clout in relation to getting hold of a courtroom for the actual hearing of an appeal so that we will have a little bit more flexibility. But with even the reduced number of appellants, it's difficult to satisfy everybody, but we will certainly attempt to do so. Now, Mr. Stojanovic, that list of your grounds of appeal hopefully will not be ten pages long, as you have suggested in your application. A notice of appeal should be succinct, to say the least of it, but we hope that you will get that on now within the time you have been granted because the Prosecution is justifiably entitled to await that document before it finalises its brief in reply, and everything is depending upon you doing that properly. Thank you very much for attending. I will now adjourn. -- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 9.41 a.m.
